transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

A flashing 'U' on a Beko induction hob almost always means it cannot detect a suitable pan. It does not necessarily mean the hob is faulty; in fact, with brand new installations, this is very commonly due to the cookware or a safety setting. Induction hobs only heat pans that are magnetic (ferrous). If your saucepan is aluminium, copper, or certain types of stainless steel that aren't magnetic, the hob will flash 'U' and refuse to heat. This is normal behaviour for induction technology. Please try these two quick checks:
1. Test the pan: Take a fridge magnet and stick it to the base of your saucepan. If it does not stick firmly, this pan will not work on any induction hob. You need a magnetic pan (cast iron or magnetic stainless steel).
2. Check for locks: Look at the display for a key symbol or padlock icon. If it is lit, press and hold that button for 3-5 seconds to unlock the controls. If you have a different pan that you know works on other zones, try placing it on this one. If the 'U' appears with a known-good magnetic pan too, then we may need to look at the hob's settings or hardware.

The magnet doesn't stick to my saucepans, but it does stick to my cast-iron casserole, and the casserole heated fine on it. I don't think the child lock is on, as the other buttons work. So is it just my pans?!

Yes, it is just your pans. The 'U' code suggests the hob cannot detect a magnetic base on those saucepans, which is why they don't heat. Since your cast-iron casserole (which is magnetic) worked perfectly, the hob itself is functioning correctly and is not faulty. You will need to use induction-compatible cookware for that zone.

candidates: Child lock or key pad engaged (medium)
Faulty induction power module for that zone (low)

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
